metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded at a 1000 Hz sampling rate from 20 participants performing tasks with visual, auditory, and combined visual-auditory cues. Participants gave self-reported vividness ratings. Data quality was validated with ERP and power spectral density analyses.

citation_details.title: Topographic Reorganization of EEG Complexity During Visual Mental Imagery: Insights from Lempel-Ziv Complexity in High-Density EEG
citation_details.author: Yu Gao, José Miguel Diniz
citation_details.abstract: Visual mental imagery is the process of reconstructing perceptual experience without sensory input. How the brain performs this process is poorly understood, particularly from the perspective of conventional linear EEG analysis. This study aims to evaluate if the two non-linear EEG complexity measures-Lempel-Ziv Complexity (LZC) and Higuchi Fractal Dimension (HFD)-can differentiate between perception and imagination and if they can be used as objective indices of neural separability of mental imagery. LZC and HFD were extracted from 62 scalp EEG channels in 46 healthy adults performing the PerceiveImagine paradigm (Li and Fan 2024), after wideband Picard ICA decomposition (1-200 Hz), which was used to make residual artefacts explicit rather than to remove components, with edge-channel EMG monitoring for artefact control. citation_details.author: Yi Yang, Ling He, Donghua Zheng, Di Wang, Yinhong An, Zhijun Yue
citation_details.venue: The International Journal of Medical Robotics and Computer Assisted Surgery
citation_details.abstract: Maintaining attention is essential for effective lower limb rehabilitation, yet repetitive exercises often cause focus loss. Existing methods lack real‐time quantitative assessment, limiting adaptive training adjustments.
